checks.title: The router runs in release mode
checks.why: Debug mode prints every registered route at startup and logs debug output per request. The route table in a log aggregator is a map of the application, and the per-request work is paid on every call for no benefit.
checks.action: Set release mode explicitly in code or through the environment on the production start path, rather than relying on the default.

verify.expect: Release mode is set for production. Nothing found means the router starts in debug mode.

checks.title: A panic in a handler cannot take the process down
checks.why: An unrecovered panic in a handler ends the whole process, not just the request, so one malformed input becomes an outage for every connected client. The convenience constructor includes recovery; building the router manually does not.
checks.action: Register recovery middleware whenever the router is constructed without it, and make sure it logs the panic rather than swallowing it.

verify.expect: Either the default constructor, or a manual router with recovery registered. A manual router without it is the finding.

checks.title: The HTTP server has read and write timeouts
checks.why: The convenience run method starts a server with no timeouts at all, so a client that opens a connection and sends a byte a minute holds a goroutine and a file descriptor indefinitely. Enough of those and the service stops accepting connections without ever looking busy.
checks.action: Construct the server explicitly with read, write and idle timeouts and pass the router as its handler, rather than using the convenience method.

verify.expect: An http.Server with timeouts set. Only a Run call, with no timeouts anywhere, is the finding.

checks.title: Trusted proxies are named rather than assumed
checks.why: By default the router trusts forwarded headers from any client, so the reported client address is whatever the caller says it is. Rate limiting, audit logs and address-based rules all become suggestions.
checks.action: Set the trusted proxy list to the addresses your load balancer actually uses, or disable proxy trust entirely if nothing sits in front.

verify.expect: The proxy list is set explicitly, to specific addresses or to nil. Nothing found means every client is trusted.

checks.title: Uploads are bounded before they reach memory
checks.why: Multipart parsing buffers a fixed amount per request in memory before spilling to disk, and the default is generous. A handful of concurrent uploads can push a small container into the platform's memory limit.
checks.action: Lower the multipart memory limit to what your endpoints actually need, and cap the request body size in middleware or at the proxy.

verify.expect: A limit is set somewhere on the path, in the application or at the proxy in front of it.
